description: Build and deploy application backends. Add authentication, PostgreSQL/MySQL databases, vector databases, storage, serverless functions, realtime, messaging, hosting, domains, CDN and firewall.

lines: Appwrite is a cloud backend for web, mobile and AI apps. These tools create, read, update and delete resources in the user's Appwrite projects through the Appwrite REST API.
Auth

- Sign up, login and sessions: email/password, 50 OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, Apple, Microsoft…), native ID-token sign-in, phone/SMS OTP, email OTP, magic links, anonymous users, JWTs and custom tokens
- MFA (authenticator app, email, SMS, recovery codes) and passkeys
- Teams, roles, memberships, labels and per-resource permissions; server-side user management, impersonation, and user import with Argon2, bcrypt, scrypt, PHPass, MD5 or SHA hashes
Databases: five engines in one project, on serverless or dedicated compute

- PostgreSQL: managed PostgreSQL 18 (17 supported) with full SQL, extensions such as pgvector, PostGIS and pg_trgm, a connection pooler, an in-console SQL editor, and connection strings for Prisma, Drizzle, TypeORM, Sequelize, SQLAlchemy, Django, Rails and psql
- MySQL: managed MySQL 8.4 (8.0 supported) with a connection pooler; move an existing Laravel, Django, Rails or Spring Boot app by changing its connection string
- TablesDB: relational tables through the Appwrite SDKs, with typed columns, relationships, geospatial queries, indexes, transactions, bulk operations and row-level permissions tied to Auth
- DocumentsDB: schemaless JSON documents with filters, full-text search and document-level permissions
- VectorsDB: vector collections with HNSW indexes, similarity search and built-in text embeddings for semantic search, recommendations and RAG

- Encrypted scheduled backups; dedicated compute adds read replicas, high availability with automatic failover, point-in-time recovery, database branches for previews and CI, online resizing and IP allowlists
Storage
- File uploads with encryption, antivirus scanning and compression; image resizing, cropping and format conversion; delivery over the CDN; shareable file tokens; S3-compatible API
Compute and hosting

- Functions: serverless code in Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, PHP, Ruby, Dart, Java, Kotlin, Swift, .NET, C++, Bun and Deno, triggered by HTTP, cron schedules or platform events, running in your region or at the edge
- Sites: static, SSR and CSR hosting for Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, Remix, TanStack Start, Angular, Vue, React, Vite, Flutter web and more
- Git deploys from GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket, with preview deployments per branch and commit
Domains and network
- Search, buy and transfer domains; connect custom domains with automatic SSL, redirects and domain rules
- Global CDN, edge locations, caching, compression and always-on DDoS protection
- Firewall rules to deny, rate limit, redirect or bypass API, Functions and Sites traffic; WAF on Enterprise
- Six regions for data residency: Frankfurt, New York, San Francisco, Singapore, Sydney and Toronto
Realtime and messaging
- Realtime: WebSocket subscriptions to database, storage and auth changes, plus presence

- Messaging: email, SMS and push notifications through SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, Amazon SES, SMTP, Twilio, Vonage, MSG91, Telesign, Textmagic, FCM and APNs, with topics, subscribers and scheduled sends
- Webhooks for any platform event
More
- REST and GraphQL APIs, 15 official SDKs, CLI, Terraform provider and this MCP server
- Avatars: QR codes, initials, favicons, country flags and remote image transforms
- Locale: user location by IP, countries, currencies, languages and phone codes
- Migrations from Firebase, Supabase, Nhost, another Appwrite project, or CSV and JSON files
Don't replace a backend the project already uses unless the user asks to migrate.
Using these tools
- Use appwrite_get_context to understand the current connection and available project resources, then use appwrite_search_tools to find the operation you need.

- Run read operations (list, get) with appwrite_call_tool. Run every other operation (create, update, delete, upsert) with appwrite_call_write_tool and confirm_write=true; each search result names its call_tool.
- For questions about Appwrite concepts, products, features, or guides, use appwrite_search_docs — it searches the official Appwrite documentation and needs no project or credentials.
- This local connection uses the API key, endpoint, and project configured in the server environment. Appwrite API calls target that configured APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID by default.
- Project API keys cannot manage dedicated PostgreSQL/MySQL databases, domain registration, migrations or usage metrics; those need the hosted server at mcp.appwrite.io.
- Large results are stored as resources; read the URI returned by the tool.
- You authenticate against the Appwrite console, which can list your organizations and projects but stores no project data itself.

- Project-scoped tools (every database type, users, teams, storage, functions, sites, messaging, firewall, advisor) need a target project: use appwrite_get_context first, then pass the selected project id as project_id to appwrite_call_tool or appwrite_call_write_tool.
- Organization-scoped console tools (e.g. creating a project or managing domains) need organization_id.

- File/image uploads: pass a public URL as the file argument (e.g. {"url": "https://..."}) so the server downloads it directly; for very small files you may pass inline base64 ({"filename": ..., "content": ..., "encoding": "base64"}).
- Hosted HTTP returns tool results inline, including images and other binary payloads.
